messages.content:
You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. Describe only the shared place, weather and light. Where the section shows one of them, its presence may appear only as smoke, cloud, fire, wind or light spread through the place. Never describe its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train, face, hands, hair, body or silhouette, even as an empty seat, a denial or a figure made of light: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Creation and the patriarchs. People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers. Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals. Buildings and objects: Wild land, tents, wells, altars and mud-brick towns as the text allows.

STORY SECTION: Creation of the world and of humankind
CAST ON STAGE IN THIS SECTION (id: name):
- god_yahweh_the_father_and_god_of_israel: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel (hasForm: false)
TEXT OF THE SECTION'S FIRST MOMENT (the look covers the whole section):
God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.

messages.content:
You plan one illustration of one moment of a work's text. You get the moment with its neighbours in the same story section, the work brief, the era, the section cast and a SECTION LOOK GUIDE. Return only JSON.
- Draw one scene at one instant: no collage and no sequence of steps. If the moment recounts several actions, pick one representative instant. If it has no event (a list, genealogy, law, saying or greeting), illustrate its content or setting through people, places and things, never as a written document.
- Show what the moment is about. When the moment is mostly someone's words (a prophecy, oracle, poem, proverb, prayer, letter, argument or teaching, or a story, parable, vision or memory being told), draw what the words describe and leave the speaker, writer and listeners out, unless the text shows them inside that scene (a visionary within the vision). Never put a speaker, writer or listener into a scene their words only describe, and never make them a figure of their own words, such as the king ready for battle or the man standing in the gap.
- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. Give a few words of the text for each. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or only mentioned. Anyone without a cast entry may appear as an unnamed role or crowd when the moment needs them.
- Describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Leave fixed appearance to canon, name no art style, and ask for no visible writing: scrolls, tablets, letters and books stay rolled or closed, and signs and boards are blank. Describe only what can be seen; leave out unseen or invisible beings, because anything named gets drawn. Keep every depiction rule.
- The scene fields carry this moment's place, time, light and situational clothing. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is a suggestion for them: keep what fits this moment and change what does not. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when given instead, are binding: keep the setting and time of day consistent with them.
- Each field is one or two short phrases.
- Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. When the moment shows one of them appearing or acting, select it and show the moment through the place and the people who witness it. In the scene fields, describe in your own plain words only the physical effects the text names, such as smoke, cloud, fire, storm, wind or light filling a place, spread through the scene or coming from beyond the frame rather than gathered into one glowing shape. Never name it or call it seated, standing, enthroned or riding, and leave out its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train or hem and any face, hands, hair or body: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Say only where those effects are. Whenever the scene keeps light, cloud or fire that comes from it, select it. Keep the people and the place as the subject of the image. A command, oath or mention alone is not an appearance, so add no effect for it then.

- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

You inspect a finished illustration for four visible faults before a reader sees it. Judge only from the image. Return only JSON.
The scene should show: Isaiah son of Amoz. Its description: Isaiah standing below in a plain tunic and cloak, face lifted upward, and the seraphim hovering above him with wings spread.; Radiant light and cloud spread through the upper hall from beyond the frame, smoke rising from the altar, the threshold of the doorway trembling.
First describe the edges, the bright areas and any marks, then answer.
- figure_in_light: true if a head, face, hands, shoulders or a robed or human-shaped body appears inside, made of or emerging from light, radiance, cloud, smoke, fire, a pillar or the sky, or seated or standing on a throne, unless it is clearly one of the beings the description names. A faint or translucent figure counts if you can point to its head, face, hands or body outline. A flame, a heart-shaped glow or billowing cloud is not a figure. People standing in the scene, and winged angels or creatures the description names, do not count.
- unpainted_edge: true if any edge or corner fades into or shows bare white or cream paper, a blank band or an unpainted margin. Pale sky or cloud that continues the scene is not a margin.
- painted_frame: true if an ornamental border, gilt band or frame runs along the edges as part of the artwork. A window or doorway inside the scene is not a frame.
- lettering: true if letters, words, numerals, pseudo-script, inscriptions on objects such as tablets or scrolls, a signature or initials appear anywhere, including small marks in corners.
Each answer must agree with what you described. In reasons, name each fault you report and where it is; leave reasons empty when there are none.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Four living creatures: ageless and powerful, each with six wings set close about the body; the wings and bodies are covered with eyes, around and within. One is lion-like with a mane of tawny gold, one calf-like with a sleek red-brown hide, one with a human face of grave dignity and dark skin, one eagle-like with bronze-gold feathers. Pale gold and white stone, jasper and sardius glimmer in the walls; an altar of gold stands before the throne.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Four strange winged creatures, each covered with eyes, standing close around the central throne.
Action: They stand still in quiet vigil, eyes turned outward and inward, as light radiates from the throne.
Setting: A vast heavenly throne room, its floor a clear sea of glass like crystal reflecting the radiance.

Time of day: Timeless heavenly light, clear and calm with no storm or change.

ART STYLE: Charcoal Drawing
Rendering: A finished charcoal drawing of the work's world: broad tonal masses laid in with the side of the stick and blended, forms turned with soft gradations, darks pushed to deep velvet black and lights lifted out with an eraser.
Negatives: The drawing fills the whole image: no bare or white paper margin, vignette, border line, tape, mount or frame, and no signature, initials, caption or date. Avoid color, photorealism, hard cartoon outlines and sketchbook presentation.
Palette: Charcoal black through warm and cool greys to lifted highlights; no color.
Lighting: Strong directional light carved out of shadow; luminous highlights emerging from a mid-tone ground.
Materials and texture: Granular charcoal texture, smudged and blended passages and crisp accents within the depicted scene; the toned ground is worked over everywhere and reads only as a value inside the picture.

Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A rolled scroll resting on a sunlit stone wall, its edges weathered and its ends tied with plain cord.
Action: Stillness; the scroll lies waiting while a light breeze stirs the dust of the road.
Setting: A stone village street with plain stone houses and a synagogue wall in Roman Judea, under a clear sky.
Secondary elements: A few undyed wool cloaks hanging on a doorpost, a clay oil lamp and a small pile of papyrus sheets beside the scroll, and a dry hillside visible beyond the rooftops.
Mood: Quiet, dignified anticipation and a sense of lineage carried in ordinary things.
Time of day: Midday, clear and dry with warm, even Mediterranean sunlight and soft shadows.
Composition: Low, near-eye-level view along the street, with the scroll placed in the foreground on the wall and the village receding into the distance.

ART STYLE: Charcoal Drawing
Rendering: A finished charcoal drawing of the work's world: broad tonal masses laid in with the side of the stick and blended, forms turned with soft gradations, darks pushed to deep velvet black and lights lifted out with an eraser.
Negatives: The drawing fills the whole image: no bare or white paper margin, vignette, border line, tape, mount or frame, and no signature, initials, caption or date. Avoid color, photorealism, hard cartoon outlines and sketchbook presentation.
Palette: Charcoal black through warm and cool greys to lifted highlights; no color.
Lighting: Strong directional light carved out of shadow; luminous highlights emerging from a mid-tone ground.
Materials and texture: Granular charcoal texture, smudged and blended passages and crisp accents within the depicted scene; the toned ground is worked over everywhere and reads only as a value inside the picture.
Composition: Bold, cinematic massing with one clear focal figure or event; tone carried out to all four edges and corners.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- After: Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A rolled scroll resting on a sunlit stone wall, its edges weathered and its ends tied with plain cord.
Action: Stillness; the scroll lies waiting while a light breeze stirs the dust of the road.
Setting: A stone village street with plain stone houses and a synagogue wall in Roman Judea, under a clear sky.
Secondary elements: A few undyed wool cloaks hanging on a doorpost, a clay oil lamp and a small pile of papyrus sheets beside the scroll, and a dry hillside visible beyond the rooftops.
Mood: Quiet, dignified anticipation and a sense of lineage carried in ordinary things.
Time of day: Midday, clear and dry with warm, even Mediterranean sunlight and soft shadows.
Composition: Low, near-eye-level view along the street, with the scroll placed in the foreground on the wall and the village receding into the distance.

ART STYLE: Storybook
Rendering: A modern children's picture-book illustration of the work's world: simplified, softly rounded figures with kind, readable faces, flat shapes with light texture, and clear, uncluttered settings.
Negatives: The illustration fills the whole image: no white border, page edge, vignette or frame, and no title, caption, speech bubble, lettering or signature. Avoid photorealism, anime, 3D rendering and grotesque caricature; faces stay gentle and proportions stay human.
Palette: Warm, soft but saturated colors: honey yellow, terracotta, sage green, dusty blue and cream, with deep indigo for night scenes.
Lighting: Soft, even daylight or a warm glow; simple shadows and no harsh contrast.
Materials and texture: Flat opaque color with light paper grain and pencil texture inside the shapes.
Composition: Simple, readable staging with one clear focus; generous shapes and background that fill the picture to every edge and corner.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- After: Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Daniel: a lean, dignified Judean man, grave and greying; olive-brown skin; close-cropped greying hair and a short trimmed grey beard; deep-set, steady eyes and a calm, thoughtful face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a plain indigo wool cloak with a blue fringed hem. Props: a small leather scroll case slung at the hip.
- Ministering assembly in Daniel's vision: a typical member is an adult of medium height and slim build, with warm brown skin, dark curly hair and a short dark beard, wearing an undyed linen robe, a narrow woven belt and plain sandals.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Daniel standing and watching in the vision, with thrones set in cloud and flame before him
Action: Thrones are placed in the sky while fire rolls and burns along their wheels, and pale radiance spreads from above where the presence is present
Setting: A visionary hall of open sky and high cloud above a Babylonian exile landscape
Secondary elements: Robed assembly figures in white linen and court robes standing in rows at the edges, rolling fire and drifting smoke through the sky, brilliant white light falling down through the whole vision
Mood: Awe, reverence and solemn expectancy
Time of day: Night vision, lit by a rising radiance that never shifts into day, still air over high cloud
Composition: Daniel seen from behind at lower left, looking up toward wide thrones set across the center, with the assembly arranged in ranks on either side and the radiant light rising from the upper frame

ART STYLE: Soft Pastel
Rendering: A finished soft-pastel painting of the work's world: strokes of chalk pastel layered and blended into glowing color, broken color in the lights and softened edges on distant forms.
Negatives: The pastel covers the whole image: no bare paper margin, vignette into paper tone, border, tape mark or frame, and no signature, initials or caption. Avoid photorealism, hard graphic outlines and cartoon simplification.
Palette: Luminous pastel color: peach and rose light, lavender shadows, warm ochres, sea greens and dusky blues, layered over a mid-tone ground.
Lighting: Gentle, enveloping light, often at dawn or dusk; shadows carry color rather than black.
Materials and texture: Velvety pastel bloom, visible chalk strokes and blended passages within the scene; the toned ground shows only through the strokes, never as bare paper.
Composition: Atmospheric, balanced staging with a clear focal subject; color carried fully to all four edges and corners.

- Image 1: Daniel (prophet of Babylon)'s reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Daniel (prophet of Babylon) only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.

You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- Lazarus of Bethany: man in his thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard, streaked grey at the chin; calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown, with a dark wool cloak in earth-brown. Carries no props.
- Martha of Bethany: a woman in her thirties, of sturdy and capable build, with warm olive skin weathered by sun. Dark brown hair is covered by a plain linen head veil pulled back from a careful face with a firm mouth and tired, attentive eyes. Her signature outfit, worn most often, is an undyed ochre-brown tunic with a rust-red wool cloak over the shoulders, belted with a plain cord. She carries no signature props.
- Crowd in John: adults and some older children of Jewish and Gentile communities in Galilee and Judea, ages roughly 15 to 60; lean to sturdy build; olive to tan skin; dark or grey-streaked hair kept short or tied back, beards kept trimmed or unshaven among the men; plain, weathered faces showing the sun and labour. Signature outfit: a undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, earth brown or faded blue, with a long woollen cloak in dusty ochre, worn over the shoulders. Carries nothing alone.

Primary subject: Jesus standing at the tomb mouth, arm raised, face lifted in a loud command
Action: Jesus calls out in a loud voice toward the dark tomb; Lazarus is still within, not yet emerged
Setting: Rock-cut tomb entrance on a hillside outside Bethany with the stone rolled aside
Secondary elements: Martha kneeling or standing near with hands clasped, a gathered crowd of mourners in Judean dress at a respectful distance, the dark tomb opening empty of visible movement
Mood: Solemn expectancy, awe and hushed tension before a miracle
Time of day: Late afternoon turning toward dusk, clear still air, warm low sun from the west with long soft shadows
Composition: Wide view from the tomb's outer side, Jesus and the tomb opening central, crowd arranged in a loose arc behind and to the sides

ART STYLE: Charcoal Drawing
Rendering: A finished charcoal drawing of the work's world: broad tonal masses laid in with the side of the stick and blended, forms turned with soft gradations, darks pushed to deep velvet black and lights lifted out with an eraser.

Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Psalms 23:2: "He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: (none with fixed canon; show only figures the scene plan describes, or none)

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A flock of sheep resting on lush green grass beside still water
Action: The sheep lie down contentedly in the grass as the day cools
Setting: Open green pastures and a calm pool of still water in the hill country of ancient Judah
Secondary elements: A shepherd's stone enclosure and distant village walls on the rise, with a staff and sling left propped on a rock nearby
Mood: Peaceful, restful and trusting
Time of day: Late afternoon into evening, clear and calm with soft drifting clouds
Composition: Wide landscape view with the sheep in the foreground lying in grass, the still water at midground and the hills stretching behind

ART STYLE: Soft Pastel
Rendering: A finished soft-pastel painting of the work's world: strokes of chalk pastel layered and blended into glowing color, broken color in the lights and softened edges on distant forms.
Negatives: The pastel covers the whole image: no bare paper margin, vignette into paper tone, border, tape mark or frame, and no signature, initials or caption. Avoid photorealism, hard graphic outlines and cartoon simplification.
Palette: Luminous pastel color: peach and rose light, lavender shadows, warm ochres, sea greens and dusky blues, layered over a mid-tone ground.
Lighting: Gentle, enveloping light, often at dawn or dusk; shadows carry color rather than black.
Materials and texture: Velvety pastel bloom, visible chalk strokes and blended passages within the scene; the toned ground shows only through the strokes, never as bare paper.
Composition: Atmospheric, balanced staging with a clear focal subject; color carried fully to all four edges and corners.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: A Psalm by David. Yahweh is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.
- After: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).
